I will do it mostly the same way I did last year, because this land is only 6 mu and I cannot gamble with it. I have done wheat and maize for many years on the same ground, and with well water I can keep the crop safe if the rain is not enough. Around here, if I cut fertilizer too much, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on a few bags. So for wheat I will use a little heavier fertilizer and more water, because wheat needs a steady stand through winter and spring. For maize after wheat, I will still feed it well, but a bit less than wheat on water. I will use improved seed like most people around me use now, because I have seen it give a fuller ear and better stand than old seed. I will keep tillage simple with rotary work, spray when I must, and aim for a safe harvest instead of saving a small amount of money and risking the crop.
